name: Shugborough inscription (1748-56)
why: Survey ("Approach per item" 31-37): "nothing mechanical decides between readings" -- 10-letter initialism, no corpus, no crib a script can check; every proposed reading (Masonic, biblical, personal) is a judgement call, not a statistic. No untried cheap test named in UNSOLVED-SURVEY.md, LANDSCAPE.md or QUEUE.md's dropped table.

name: Zodiac Z13 and Z32
why: Z13's one on-record mechanism (the poster's ARTHUR LA keyboard scheme) was already stress-tested with a matched random-string control on 24 Sept 2026 (ciphers/zodiac-z13-stress/, status closed-negative of the mechanism only: whole-family control hits a name7 96.8% of the time, so ARTHUR+LA is inside chance, not above it). No other named, untried, disk-first cheap test exists for Z13 or Z32 in the repo; Z340 (a different item) is already solved (survey row 32) and excluded from the ranking.

name: Kryptos K4
why: UNSOLVED-SURVEY.md row 33 and the "Approach per item" 31-37 section: "for Kryptos... none" as an untried cheap test, and the plaintext was recovered from Sanborn's own papers Sept 2025 (Kobek, Byrne, Smithsonian AAA) and sold at auction 20 Nov 2025 -- cryptanalysis is moot; the open question (matching Sanborn's key to the public ciphertext) is not a $3/30-min disk test.

name: Beale cryptograms (1885 pamphlet)
why: Survey: "hoax per Schmeh, Bourdeau"; no untried cheap test named. B1 (520 numbers) and B3 (618 numbers) have had decades of book-cipher key searches; nothing on disk in this repo proposes a specific untried key text or method.

name: Rohonc Codex
why: Survey: Kiraly and Tokai's code-system reading (Cryptologia 42:4, 2018) is the state of the art and "needs Hungarian and years, not a cheap test." 448 pages, no machine-checkable statistic proposed anywhere in the repo.

name: Codex Seraphinianus
why: Survey row 36 and QUEUE.md: "not a cipher by the author's statement" (Luigi Serafini has said the script is asemic, invented without meaning). Nothing to test.

name: Voynich manuscript
why: Survey: Bourdeau assesses it as "not a cipher of a European language"; QUEUE.md's dropped table repeats the same adjudication. 240 pages, decades of heavy-compute effort by many groups; no specific untried cheap test is named in the repo.

name: WW2 pigeon message (Bletchingley)
why: sources/schmeh/posts/20-pigeon.txt on disk. Survey row 38 and QUEUE.md's dropped table: GCHQ's own published assessment is a one-time pad, cryptanalytically unbreakable without the pad itself, which is not held. No cheap test can move an OTP.

name: Double Column Transposition "reloaded" challenge (MysteryTwister)
why: QUEUE.md dropped table: "artificial compute challenges, not historical ciphers" (grouped with rank 40). No ciphertext is on disk in this repo; this is a designed cryptographic challenge (known cipher family, unknown key), not a historical-document cryptanalysis target, and out of this project's scope per CLAUDE.md Pipeline 3.

name: Schmeh's 65-bit world-record challenge
why: Brief's own worked example; QUEUE.md dropped table groups it with rank 39 as an "artificial compute challenge." A 65-bit key-search is a hardware/distributed-compute project (per Schmeh's own framing, "world record"), not a $3 Sonnet cheap test.

name: Bonus 22 (M-209 series, Bouchaudy's challenge site)
why: Survey: "Lasry's method exists" (a published ciphertext-only M-209 attack), but no m209 tool, key-space search or matched-control harness exists anywhere in tools/ or ciphers/ in this repo (grepped tools/, ciphers/, QUEUE.md: no hits for m209, M-209, Bonus 22 or Bouchaudy). Implementing a ciphertext-only M-209 hill-climb from scratch is a campaign-scale build, not a disk-first $3/30-min breadth test; the ciphertext itself is not fetched (this brief is disk-only, no host access). Worth a named campaign-lane brief later citing Lasry's published method, not a breadth spec.
